articles.body: Annette Young is pleased to welcome Alain Greilsammer, Professor of Political Science at Bar-Ilan University in Tel Aviv. In the wake of the October 7 attacks, regional tensions with Iran, and deepening domestic divisions, Greilsammer argues that the election will be fundamentally shaped by concerns over democratic accountability, judicial independence and the unequal distribution of civic obligations. He warns Netanyahu’s policies risk transforming Israel into “something like an authoritarian or non-democratic state.” He suggests that Israel’s Arab political parties could play a decisive role in determining the election’s outcome.

articles.body: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Ibrahim Abu Ahmad, Author, Palestinian Israeli political and peace activist and Head of Social Media for Israel's left-wing Democrats. “Currently, the sentiment in Israel is built around fear and trauma,” explains Ahmad. His most striking observation concerns the apparent contradiction between political leadership and public sentiment: “Many want to see an Arab-Jewish coalition. It's the leadership that is afraid to say it.” Ultimately, he moves beyond conventional electoral calculations to frame Arab-Jewish partnership as a question of democratic survival.
articles.headline: Ibrahim Abu Ahmad on Israeli election: 'Crucial for Arab citizens to have ally in Jewish community'

articles.body: A list of academics, engineers, artists and activists chosen by Serbia’s student assemblies defeated long-ruling president Aleksandar Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party Sunday. The shock victory comes after nearly two years of student-led anti-corruption protests – and may serve as a model for other movements hoping to turn street demonstrations into concrete political change.
articles.headline: How student assemblies brought down the Serbian government

articles.body: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Ron Gerlitz, CEO of aChord Center at Hebrew University, an Israeli organization specialising in the social psychology of intergroup relations. “The main issue in this election is the fight for Israeli democracy,” explains Gerlitz. And beneath the struggle over democratic institutions lies the erosion of Benjamin Netanyahu's longstanding association with national security. Gerlitz also examines the psychological foundations of Netanyahu's enduring support, the influence of conspiracy narratives, the electoral significance of Arab parties and the uncertain future of the two-state solution.
articles.headline: Israeli elections a 'referendum' on Netanyahu, security and whether Israel will 'remain a democracy'

articles.body: Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Tuesday came as close to the campaign trail as he’s been all year. And even then, he tried to stay just offshore. Rubio appeared with President Donald Trump in Corpus Christi, Texas, as he rallied alongside an oil tanker carrying Venezuelan crude. The visit helped spotlight a proud White House accomplishment — toppling the Venezuelan dictator Nicolás Maduro and opening the country’s energy supply — in a political battleground state. The unexpected nature of Rubio’s presence, after the president coaxed him up on stage during the rally, is likely enough to shield the nation’s top diplomat from allegations that he is interfering in the midterm campaign. The former Florida senator has kept a careful distance from partisan politics, even as colleagues like Attorney General Todd Blanche have defied longstanding norms against some administration officials engaging in electioneering. “It's an honor to work for the greatest country in the world, for the greatest president in the history of the United States of America,” Rubio said in brief remarks from the stage. “We love you, Texas.” A White House official, who like others in this article was granted anonymity to share details of the trip, said that Rubio was backstage during the rally when the president brought him up and that he was only there in his capacity as national security adviser, not to stump ahead of the midterms. While Rubio, who was not expected to speak at the event, has maintained the tradition of secretaries of State not campaigning, Republicans have been clamoring for the potential 2028 presidential hopeful to do so, seeing him as one of the party’s strongest messengers in a bruising midterm cycle in which they have been desperate for any additional help. One GOP official in a state with a key Senate race, granted anonymity to share private conversations, said that they asked for Rubio to attend a recent political event but were told the secretary of State wasn't doing political events given his role as chief diplomatic officer. “Rubio is Trump’s best asset, and they know they are in a dog fight to win in Texas,” said Bill Cortese, a GOP operative who has advised Rep. Elise Stefanik (R-N.Y.). Even if Rubio had not come up on stage, “news of Rubio simply being in the state could potentially boost the GOP’s chances in places that they need it.” Plus, the secretary of State had another good reason for being there: Rubio was one of the central architects of the administration’s Venezuela strategy and has been a leading figure in managing the country’s political transition and economic arrangements with the U.S. in the wake of Maduro’s ouster. “It’s his win and his deal,” a Trump administration official added about Rubio and the Venezuela link. Asked why Rubio accompanied Trump on the Texas trip, the White House referred to one of Trump’s Truth Social posts from August in which he credited Rubio and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth for negotiating the oil deal with Venezuela. A State Department spokesperson noted Rubio’s role as national security adviser and said that he “needs time with the president on all kinds of issues. The president will be on the go, so being on the plane with him gives him a chance to talk to him about these items.” The secretary of State notably skipped the Republican National Committee’s midterm convention in Dallas last month, opting instead to go on a diplomatic trip to Colombia. “Marco loves campaigns and politics and he cares desperately about making sure that the House and Senate remain in Republican hands, but I think he also realizes that part of being secretary of State is you don’t engage in overt political activity,” said a person close to Rubio. In Trump’s first term, Secretary of State Mike Pompeo broke with tradition and made a handful of public appearances that directly or indirectly appeared campaign related, including delivering remarks to the Republican National Convention in 2020. On a practical level, most secretaries of State travel overseas so much that it’s hard to spare time for campaigns. But Rubio travels more infrequently than his predecessors, in part because of his national security adviser role, which keeps him at the White House. And Rubio also has a more nontraditional role even as secretary of State, focusing most of his energy on Latin America while the president’s special envoys, including Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, have handled negotiations to try to end the wars in Iran, Ukraine and Gaza. Yet the Texas visit — in which Trump sought to link one of his signature foreign policy accomplishments with efforts to reduce prices — came as a relief to the Republicans who believe Rubio is one of the party’s most trusted messengers on the economy and have for months wanted to see him on the trail. Results from The POLITICO Poll suggest Rubio can be a useful surrogate on the campaign trail. Across three polls this month, Republican midterm voters consistently selected Rubio as their third-highest choice to hit the campaign trail to help their party, behind Trump and Vice President JD Vance but ahead of Texas Sen. Ted Cruz, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and others. Support for Rubio on the campaign trail is also fairly steady across Trump’s 2024 coalition, with only an 8-point gap between the MAGA base (31%) and non-MAGA Trump voters (23%) saying the secretary of State would help Republicans if he campaigned. Meanwhile, MAGA loyalists were significantly more likely than non-MAGA Trump voters to support Trump and Vance hitting the trail. Notably, Rubio also generates less negative backlash than other figures. Democrats widely support the impeachment of Trump, Vance, Kennedy and others. But support for impeaching Rubio is lower than the other figures, pushing overall public opinion against impeachment. “Marco Rubio is Republicans’ most valuable asset in this difficult environment. While he has broad support from the MAGA base, he also appeals to centrist voters and obviously to critical Hispanic voters. It makes sense that they would find a way to activate him,” said former Florida Rep. Carlos Curbelo. Kimberly Leonard, Alex Gangitano and Seb Wride, chief pollster at PF Global, contributed to this report.
articles.headline: Republicans wanted Rubio on the stump. Trump coaxed him there.

articles.body: Republicans’ small-dollar donor base has contracted in recent years, leaving the party more dependent on a tiny group of wealthy megadonors for support. The GOP has had a cash advantage all year thanks to a relatively small group of large donors who have funded super PACs — Elon Musk alone has given nearly half a billion dollars this cycle. But the campaigns themselves have raised relatively little, and there’s one major reason: Other than President Donald Trump, who is still the party’s biggest fundraiser, Republicans still haven’t figured out how to raise money online. New campaign finance filings reveal just how deep the problem goes. While Republicans have long struggled to grow their grassroots donor base, they’ve moved in the wrong direction in recent years. The number of federal donors giving through WinRed, the major GOP online fundraising platform, is down, with roughly 1.5 million donors so far this cycle compared to 2.2 million at this time in 2022. Meanwhile the number of donors has increased by about one third on ActBlue, from 4.9 million to roughly 6.6 million. The contrast is stark: A single Democratic candidate, James Talarico in Texas, has had roughly the same number of donors on ActBlue this cycle as all Republican candidates and committees combined had on WinRed, according to a POLITICO analysis of reports ActBlue and WinRed submitted to the Federal Election Commission. Republican digital strategists who have been sounding the alarm for years say lagging donations are a product of fatigue, driven by years of urgent messages to the same set of potential donors. “We beat the absolute hell out of low-dollar donors with texts and emails without expanding our [donor lists], and now no one pays attention,” said Wesley Donehue, a South Carolina-based GOP digital strategist. Republicans’ online fundraising struggles have put their House and Senate candidates at a particular disadvantage, as candidates — unlike super PACs — face strict contribution limits and need a far larger pool of donors from which to raise money. Poor candidate fundraising has major campaign implications: Democrats’ cash advantage on that front has helped them run nearly as many ads as Republicans despite having less money overall, because candidates and parties get better rates than super PACs on broadcast TV. Democrats’ grassroots fundraising strength is in part because of how decentralized the party is, with individual campaigns and groups building their own donor lists and fundraising operations. Virtually all of the the top Democratic fundraisers online this year are Senate candidates in competitive races. But Republicans’ online fundraising, like so much of the party, is still centered around Trump and the official party committees. Unlike on the Democratic side, few individual Republicans have managed to break out. Republicans’ fundraising troubles have left them more reliant on Trump: The president’s super PAC, MAGA Inc., is among the biggest midterm spenders . The group and its affiliates have now spent $296 million — after facing pressure for much of the cycle from some in the GOP who wished it would have gotten involved sooner . “Candidates are not investing the time and resources in programs that grow the donor lists and attract their supporters into the ecosystem. Instead, they just barrage previous donors with ongoing requests for donation,” said Eric Wilson, a longtime Republican digital strategist and executive director of the Center for Campaign Innovation. “Credit to the Trump team — they brought new people into the ecosystem, and those people continue to give to them.” Trump has continued to fundraise since returning to the White House, including through his Never Surrender leadership PAC, which was formed out of his 2024 campaign committee, and two joint fundraising committees from his previous presidential runs. Of the nearly 1.5 million donors who have given on WinRed this cycle, 324,000 of them — a bit over 22% — have given only to Trump’s groups through the platform but not any other candidate or committee, POLITICO’s analysis found. Another 39% of WinRed donors have given to both Trump and another Republican. Overall, that means about 3 in 5 WinRed donors this cycle have given to Trump, when he is neither on the ballot nor able to run for president again. That’s left non-Trump GOP donors in the clear minority just as the party begins to look for a new standard bearer ahead of 2028. WinRed isn’t the only online GOP fundraising platform, but it is by far the largest and features all of the major party committees along with prominent House and Senate candidates across the map. Its FEC reports include only federal candidates and committees, not those in state-level races or nonprofits that use the platform. Republicans once saw their online fundraising disadvantages as a matter of technology. ActBlue, which has been around since the 2000s, gave Democrats a major fundraising advantage in the late 2010s, at a time when Republicans had no similar centralized platform. WinRed, which launched in 2019, aimed to counter that. Now strategists say the GOP’s infrastructure has come a long way, but the party’s tactics still lag behind. Democratic candidates eyeing higher office often maintain large fundraising operations, which they can use to raise money on behalf of candidates in battleground races while also building their own lists. Among the top 20 ActBlue fundraisers this cycle are former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg’s leadership PAC and Sen. Mark Kelly’s (D-Ariz.) campaign committee. Kelly leveraged GOP attacks on his military service earlier this cycle to boost both his own fundraising and help Democrats across the map . Wilson, the GOP strategist, credited out-of-cycle Democrats for building strong lists that they could use to shore up other candidates. The Republican side, he said, lacks similar coordination. “Any time a Democrat announces they're running for reelection, that week every Democrat in the Senate is sending a message to their list raising money for that person,” he said. About the analysis: Donation totals and number of donors are based on ActBlue and WinRed receipts from all reports this cycle, covering Jan. 1, 2025, through Oct. 14, 2026. Donations that were later refunded are still included. POLITICO’s analysis identifies unique donors based on matching full names and zip codes.
articles.headline: The hidden GOP fundraising weakness is getting worse

articles.body: 🚨🚨MUST READ🚨🚨: Mayor Zohran Mamdani and a group of fellow basketball enthusiasts have been secretly using the NYPD Police Academy’s gymnasium in Queens to play pickup ball, according to four people familiar with the games. The mayor and his crew typically show up around 10 or 11 p.m. and enter surreptitiously through a loading dock before hitting the court. While sports fanaticism has often buoyed the political brand of past mayors, Mamdani’s choice of venue is raising eyebrows. Read the story from POLITICO’s Graham Rayman, Chris Sommerfeldt and Joe Anuta here . FINANCE FLAWS: Republican gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman’s campaign finance disclosure reports have been plagued by inaccuracies since the spring. Copies of the campaign’s bank statements obtained by POLITICO suggest his filings might have even more problems than previously suspected. According to a disclosure report submitted to the state Board of Elections earlier this month, the Blakeman campaign had only $178,000 in the bank as of Sept. 28. Yet the campaign’s checking account had a balance of $1.7 million on Sept. 28, according to TD Bank’s monthly statement. The bank records also show dozens of transactions that are missing from his campaign finance filings. On July 29, for example, the bank statements identified the campaign using a check with the number 1156 to make a $13,500 payment to an unspecified recipient. Yet Blakeman’s campaign finance reports do not identify any transactions that used check number 1156. It also hasn’t shown a single payment totaling $13,500 at any point over the past year. In addition, there are instances in which the bank records show apparent contributions to the campaign that never show up in the disclosure reports. The statements show Blakeman was wired $18,000 by actress Lois Robbins on Sept. 2, for example, while the filings don’t show any transactions totaling $18,000 within two weeks of that date or any donations from Robbins. An $18,000 wire from attorney and campaign finance chair Howard Fensterman in July similarly doesn’t match anything in the disclosure reports. Blakeman is the first gubernatorial candidate in state history to participate in the new matching funds program that lets him receive up to $3.5 million in public money. Then-Mayor Eric Adams was blocked from participating in a similar New York City program last year due to discrepancies between his bank statements and disclosure reports. Reinvent Albany’s Kyle Kennedy said he didn’t know the cause of the discrepancies, but that it could just be due to “the timing of when things were recorded.” But, he noted, Blakeman’s campaign “will automatically be audited by the Board of Elections after the election. … Campaign finance enforcement takes place after elections, not in real-time.” Blakeman’s campaign didn’t respond to a request to explain the discrepancies. It has previously said its campaign finance problems are due to technical issues caused by a large number of donors. Several of the candidate’s campaign finance disclosure reports have been repeatedly amended, often in ways that made the initial numbers wildly inaccurate. His July report showed him with $4.7 million in the bank; that was changed a week later to show his balance was $6.1 million; then in August it was changed to $4.3 million. As POLITICO reported earlier this month , Blakeman has received about $360,000 in donations over the contribution limit that he still needs to return. Many of the donations he has already returned have been highly unusual — one person who gave $1 in July was quickly refunded $780.76. His campaign then said he accidentally submitted some duplicate contributions. Nearly a month later, it hasn’t amended the filing to show which transactions were real. And as New York Focus reported , the Blakeman campaign submitted requests to receive matching funds for 2,600 donations that were ineligible for matches. From the Capitol THE WEEKEND TURNOUT: Early voting turnout has skyrocketed in every corner of the state, according to unofficial tallies provided by the state Board of Elections. On the first two days of early voting in 2022, 261,735 people cast a ballot. This weekend, that number increased to 485,205 — a jump of roughly 85 percent. The biggest increases were in the North Country — particularly in the congressional seat being vacated by Rep. Elise Stefanik, which is now a battleground district for the first time in over a decade. Washington County’s weekend turnout was up 236 percent from four years ago. Early voting increased 196 percent in St. Lawrence County, 182 percent in Warren County, and 179 percent in Herkimer County. The smallest gains were in the Hudson Valley. That was especially true in the district held by Democratic Rep. Pat Ryan, where early turnout was the highest in the state four years ago as Ryan won his first full term in a nail-biter. His race isn’t widely viewed as competitive this year, and the smallest increase among the state’s 62 counties was in Ulster, which was up only 41 percent relative to 2022. There were also relatively middling gains in Erie County (up 60 percent) and Nassau County (up 64 percent). Those are the places where New York’s two gubernatorial candidates live, perhaps indicating that neither is yet the beneficiary of any outpourings of hometown pride. — Bill Mahoney FROM THE CAMPAIGN TRAIL ORDER’S UP: Republican Rep. Mike Lawler spent part of this afternoon working at McDonald’s in Haverstraw – a potential backup job “if things don’t work out in November,” he said while putting on his uniform. Lawler is in the final campaign stretch in one of the country’s most closely watched congressional battlegrounds against Democrat Cait Conley. The lawmaker spent his McDonald’s shift cooking food, handing out orders and speaking with constituents – one of whom openly admitted to voting against him before taking their food and driving off. Aside from that one outlier, customers gave Lawler a warm reception at the drive-thru window. The visit was seemingly part of an effort to make inroads in Haverstraw, a town that leans Democratic. Lawler told POLITICO he’s feeling confident going into the final days of his campaign, but insisted that he is an underdog in the Hudson Valley district. In the 2024 presidential election, Kamala Harris and Lawler each won the district. “I feel very good about where we are heading on Election Day. Eight days from now, we’re going to win because I’ve done the work,” Lawler said in an interview. “I’ve delivered for my district, and the people here know me. I’m from here; I’ve lived here my whole life, I know the community..” And for those wondering about Lawler’s go-to McDonald’s order: double quarter-pounder with cheese, a Coke and a four-piece McNugget. — Katelyn Cordero STUMPING SPRINT: Fresh off a weekend of enthusiastic campaigning for Gov. Kathy Hochul , the mayor addressed reporters at a press conference this morning. He stuck to his rhetoric touting the governor as a champion for affordable child care and lampooning her GOP foe Bruce Blakeman as a Trump puppet. The mayor was also pressed about whether he expects something in return for all the campaigning he’s been doing for Hochul — such as increased taxes on the rich, a top goal for Mamdani and his democratic socialist allies in the state Legislature. “I’m expecting a continuation of a positive and productive working relationship with the governor,” he said. “I’m excited for that relationship to continue. It’s been one that’s delivered for working class New Yorkers, and I’m confident it’s going to keep delivering.” It’s far from an explicit commitment, but it suggests he’ll continue pushing Hochul for tax hikes should she win reelection — something City Council Speaker Julie Menin told POLITICO she would support to bankroll child care programs earlier this month. Mamdani also repeatedly mentioned the importance of showing New Yorkers that a mayor and a governor can have a productive working relationship — an apparent dig at the storied feud between former Mayor Bill de Blasio and former Governor Andrew Cuomo . “New Yorkers across the five boroughs are excited about us finally working together, where they haven’t seen mayors and governors do that often in the past to be able to deliver on common sense things,” he said. — Molly Reinmann FROM CITY HALL GRAND PLANS: Mamdani’s chief of staff Elle Bisgaard-Church laid out the democratic socialist administration’s governing philosophy today — including its opposition to means-testing for government programs. “We look especially to universal social programs, facilitating forms of collective ownership, supporting the growth of unions. In short, creating shared economic security and stability through material programs,” Bisgaard-Church said at an event on Mamdani’s affordability agenda hosted by the New York City Policy Forum, a left-leaning research and publishing network. “On the contrary, means-tested programs segregate and encumber people.” She pointed to other periods in the city’s history that saw “rich public institutions that could compete with the private sector,” citing NYCHA, the MTA and CUNY. Public housing, in particular, has seen significant deterioration in recent decades amid federal disinvestment. Reversing that trajectory is one of the most pressing issues Mamdani faces as mayor. “Today we are governed by rules of austerity and face a withered welfare regime, means-tested policies, decayed public sector, and weakened public institutions,” Bisgaard-Church continued. “These are the political realities our administration wants to overturn, and we know that tackling the crushing cost of living is again key to doing so.” The event drew other top Mamdani officials including Deputy Mayor for Housing and Planning Leila Bozorg, Economic Development Corporation Chair Lina Khan, and Consumer and Worker Protection Commissioner Sam Levine. — Janaki Chadha IN OTHER NEWS — HOMELESSNESS: Mamdani’s early efforts to address a ballooning homelessness problem in the city have largely failed, community leaders allege. ( The Wall Street Journal ) — SUNNYSIDE YARD: Housing experts weighed in on the outlandishly high cost of Mamdani and Trump’s proposed development at Sunnyside Yard. ( The City Reporter ) — BK DEMS: There are four state legislative seats Democrats are looking to flip in southern Brooklyn this midterm cycle, a fact that has largely been overshadowed by the party’s drama-packed leadership succession saga. articles.body: House Democrats are pushing into redder and redder territory. History shows those last-minute moves don’t usually pan out, even in favorable cycles. Since 2018, Democrats haven’t flipped any Republican-held seat that was added to the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee’s “Red to Blue” list in the September or October before Election Day, according to a POLITICO analysis. Of the 28 total candidates from 2018 to 2024 that were added in the final two months of the campaign, just three Democrats won — all in Democratic-held open seats. That’s a much lower rate than average Red to Blue performance. Out of 203 candidates added to the program in the four previous cycles, 73 flipped their seats. That’s not a shock: The DCCC tends to add the biggest reaches later as it moves through the cycle, both to make sure its best opportunities are funded first and have enough attention and to try to create a sense of momentum and map expansion for donors and the media. In fact, the DCCC used some of the seats in their latest round of additions in a recent fundraising plea sent out by Executive Director Julie Merz, who warned that without more cash the committee “could be leaving winnable races on the table.” But it illuminates how hard it is — even in the best of environments — to reach deep into red territory in order to flip House seats. And it’s especially true now, as the House battlefield has shrunk significantly since 2018 because of gerrymandering. Since the beginning of September, the DCCC has added nine Democrats to Red to Blue: independent Bill Hill in AK-AL; Will Lawrence in MI-07; Mitchell Berman in WI-01; Chris Jones in AR-02; Dwayne Romero in CO-03; Eliott Rodriguez in FL-27; Teresa Benitez-Thompson in NV-02; Blake Gendebien in NY-21; and Justin Pearson in TN-09. Democrats acknowledge these late additions are a low-percentage play. Former DCCC staffer Cole Leiter, who worked there for the 2018 and 2020 cycles, said the committee recruits and tracks reach-district candidates early in the cycle with hopes the political winds will shift their way. “That is an investment in the unpredictability of the map,” Leiter said. “Most of these seats probably won’t flip, but one or two might.” Regardless of whether or not Democrats ultimately win the seats they’ve added late this year (the DCCC added six deep-red targets to Red to Blue in early October) — the additions alone contribute to a narrative of a party on offense. And they can also be a boon for fundraising for those specific candidates as well as to entice donors with exactly which areas their dollars will go if they pony up. “Even if there's ultimately not a massive success rate in those final editions, it is not a bad thing to make sure that those campaigns have any last-minute dollars that the designation can bring,” said Meredith Kelly, a former DCCC staffer who worked the 2016 and 2018 cycles. “Just make sure that they have a surfboard in the water and have an ability to potentially take advantage of a really, really good night.” This cycle’s late-add Democrats are almost all facing cash disadvantages against their incumbent GOP opponents. Of the nine Democrats added within the past two months, only one — Benitez-Thompson, running against Republican David Flippo — has reported more cash on hand than their opponent. Five of them are facing fundraising deficits of over $1 million, according to Federal Election Commission filings. Democrats’ poor record in these seats is somewhat self-selecting — seats added to the program late in the cycle reflect the fact that Democrats weren’t initially convinced they could be flipped. Whitney Fox, who lost by 9 points to GOP Rep. Anna Paulina Luna in FL-13 in 2024 and was among the last Democrats to be added to Red to Blue when she was picked in late September, said her campaign suffered from the delay in adding her to the program, even as she acknowledged the DCCC is forced to make strategic decisions with limited resources. The late additions also limit the window that candidates can capitalize on the program’s benefits. After initially being told she wouldn’t be added and after what she said was months of making her case to the DCCC, Fox made the list just before Hurricane Milton devastated the Tampa area, which she said made it difficult to fundraise off her newly minted Red to Blue status. “I felt like it was too little, too late,” she said. The Democrat running against Luna this cycle, Leela Gray, was added to Red to Blue in late August. Fox, who is informally advising local Florida candidates this cycle, said she offered Gray advice on how to make the list early. “I was a squeaky wheel trying to talk to leadership and Democratic members of Congress, and then it got to a certain point where I was no longer the squeaky wheel,” she said she relayed to Gray. “I was going to take the spoke off the wheel and hit people over the head with it.” Still the DCCC believes this cycle will be different, history be damned. And if recent national polling showing them with a double-digit lead in the generic ballot is correct, some of these late additions might break through. “Records are meant to be broken,” DCCC spokesperson Viet Shelton said in a statement. “We’re on track to break them this year because across the battlefield, we’ve got amazing recruits and the enthusiasm to fire House Republicans for making life unaffordable is off the charts.” A version of this article first appeared in POLITICO Pro’s Morning Score. articles.body: <p>La reforma de la ley de seguridad ciudadana, la conocida por sus detractores como <i>ley mordaza</i>, se ha convertido en la eterna asignatura pendiente de todos los gobiernos de Pedro Sánchez. Siempre prometida, pero nunca alcanzada. Durante la legislatura a la que acaba de poner fin el adelanto electoral, el proyecto ha navegado en una marejada de discrepancias entre los partidos que apoyan cambiar la norma hasta desembocar en una zozobra que se vislumbraba desde hace meses. A pesar de que, en octubre de 2024, el proyecto pasó su primer trámite parlamentario, en los dos años transcurridos desde entonces no ha llegado a reunirse la ponencia ―grupo de parlamentarios que estudian los proyectos legislativos antes de su envío a comisión y, si es aprobado, a pleno― precisamente por las diferencias entre los partidos que debían sumar sus votos para sacar adelante la iniciativa: PSOE, Sumar, EH Bildu, PNV, ERC, Podemos y Junts. Es la tercera vez que se frustra la reforma. En 2019, la causa fue la disolución anticipada de las Cortes. Y en 2023, el acuerdo sobre el texto entre socialistas, Unidas Podemos y los nacionalistas vascos fue rechazado por ERC, Junts, EH Bildu y BNG al considerarlo insuficiente.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-28/la-eterna-asignatura-pendiente-de-reformar-la-ley-mordaza.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>La Policía ha identificado a 24 agentes “dinamizadores” que estuvieron en Marruecos guiando supuestamente a miles de migrantes el día 30 de julio, cuando una multitud de unas 80.000 personas logró cruzar la frontera. Los documentos y vídeos que el Centro Nacional de Inmigración y Fronteras (CENIF) ha entregado a la jueza de la Audiencia Nacional demuestran la pasividad de los gendarmes marroquíes ese día, con actitud de brazos caídos o, en algún caso, señalando el camino hacia la ciudad autónoma. Los agentes tratan de esclarecer la identidad exacta de todos ellos y, de momento, han logrado tomar declaración a un exmiembro de la gendarmería y a dos migrantes que han situado a varias autoridades del país en la frontera el día de los hechos investigados. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-27/la-policia-identifica-a-24-agentes-dinamizadores-en-ceuta-a-traves-de-videos-y-fotografias-analizadas.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>Una quincena de representantes de nueve <a href="https://elpais.com/noticias/sindicatos-policiales/" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/noticias/sindicatos-policiales/">sindicatos de la Policía Nacional y asociaciones profesionales de la Guardia Civil</a> se han encerrado a última hora de la tarde de este martes en la sede del Ministerio del Interior como medida de presión tras suspender el departamento de Fernando Grande-Marlaska el diálogo que desde hace meses mantenían ambas partes para mejorar las condiciones de jubilación de los agentes. “Tras romperse las negociaciones con la Secretaría de Estado de Seguridad [SES, que encabeza Aina Calvo], representantes sindicales y de asociaciones profesionales permanecen en un encierro pacífico e indefinido en la SES, para exigir una solución a nuestra jubilación”, han informado a través de un comunicado Justicia Policial (Jupol), el Sindicato Unificado de Policía (SUP), la Unión Federal de Policía (UFP), la Asociación Unificada de Guardias Civiles (AUGC), Justicia para la Guardia Civil (Jucil), la Asociación de Escala de Suboficiales de la Guardia Civil (ASESGC), Asociación Profesional de Cabos, Independientes de la Guardia Civil (IGC) y la Asociación Española de Guardias Civiles (AEGC). articles.body: <p>El juez Santiago Pedraz ha acordado este martes que el coronel Antonio Balas, jefe del Departamento de Investigación Económica y Anticorrupción de la Unidad Central Operativa (UCO) de la Guardia Civil, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-16/interior-evita-el-choque-y-asume-que-balas-siga-al-frente-de-las-investigaciones-que-afectan-al-psoe.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-16/interior-evita-el-choque-y-asume-que-balas-siga-al-frente-de-las-investigaciones-que-afectan-al-psoe.html">siga al frente del <i>caso Leire Díez</i></a><i> </i>“con carácter permanente”, ante el riesgo de que su reciente ascenso suponga en el futuro su salida de la unidad <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-31/interior-enfrenta-el-futuro-papel-del-jefe-anticorrupcion-de-la-uco-ante-su-inminente-ascenso.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-31/interior-enfrenta-el-futuro-papel-del-jefe-anticorrupcion-de-la-uco-ante-su-inminente-ascenso.html">rumbo a otro destino en el instituto armado</a>. El magistrado de la Audiencia Nacional argumenta su decisión en que estas pesquisas, en las que se investiga una presunta trama liderada por la exmilitante socialista Leire Díez y el ex secretario de Organización del PSOE Santos Cerdán dedicada a torpedear causas judiciales que afectan al Gobierno o al entorno familiar de Pedro Sánchez, son de una “extraordinaria complejidad”, tienen una “especial trascendencia institucional y jurídica” y el actual estado de las mismas hace necesario “garantizar su continuidad, integridad, eficacia, reserva e imparcialidad” hasta su conclusión.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-27/el-juez-pedraz-blinda-la-continuidad-del-coronel-balas-al-frente-del-caso-leire-hasta-su-conclusion.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: Manolo González ha estat cessat com a entrenador de l’Espanyol . Abans, però hi havia molta expectació per escoltar la roda de premsa del gallec després de caure contra el Sestao River a la Copa del Rei i el discurs ha estat un comiat. S’ha vist un tècnic molt afectat, amb un tarannà de desil·lusió en què ha reconegut que no vol pensar en el seu possible acomiadament, però que, efectivament, estat el seu darrer partit . Manolo González, taxatiu: “És un dels pitjors dies de la meva vida” Al tècnic de l’Espanyol li han preguntat directament si aquest partit serà la cloenda de la seva etapa a la banqueta blanc-i-blava: “Sí, a mi em sap molt de greu, la veritat, perquè m’estimo molt el club . Penso que hem fet una gran feina durant , el que tu dius, dos anys i mig , aconseguint objectius, i acabar amb un partit així, em sap molt de greu, la veritat, molt, molt de greu perquè crec que no és just per tot el que s’ha fet, per tota la feina que s’ha aconseguit i a mi em sap molt, molt de greu, la veritat, i és una llàstima .” Manolo González ha criticat que l’equip hagi encaixat dos gols a pilota aturada i assegura que no pots tenir aquestes “errades de concentració”. Preguntat sobre una possible dimissió, el gallec ha dit que no pensa en això: “ Estic molt fotut pel partit, molt fotut, és un dia dels pitjors de la meva vida i ara mateix no estic ni pensant en això” Manolo no ha descartat que la seva etapa s’hagi acabat aquí abans de fer-se oficial: “Pot ser, la veritat. Però no sé que passarà aquesta nit o demà”. “Ara mateix vull estar una estona tranquil, reflexionar, pensar, i ja veurem què passa demà quan arribem , però ara mateix el que vull és estar una mica tranquil, estic bastant tocat, fotut”, ha afegit. També et pot interessar Manolo González: “Sé que la meva situació corre perill” Roger Matamoros i Aparicio 2 minuts de lectura

articles.body: Manolo González ha estat acomiadat després de caure contra el Sestao River (4-3) en la primera eliminatòria de la Copa del Rei. OFICIAL | Manolo González deixa de ser entrenador de l' #RCDE . El Club vol agrair-li la seva feina durant tots aquests anys i li desitja molta sort en els seus projectes futurs. — RCD Espanyol de Barcelona (@RCDEspanyol) October 27, 2026 El fins ara tècnic perico ha estat destituït amb l’equip blanc-i-blau eliminat de la competició del KO i en divuitena posició de la Lliga, a un punt de la salvació. La ratxa és demolidora: han sumat 1 punt dels darrers 15. També et pot interessar Les darreres paraules de Manolo González a l’Espanyol: “És el pitjor dia de la meva vida” Pablo Agudo 2 minuts de lectura El RCD Espanyol ha fet oficial la destitució de Manolo González . La decisió ha estat presa després de la eliminació de l’equip perico en la primera eliminatòria de la Copa del Rei. Va agafar l’equip a Segona Divisió al març del 2024 i el va tornar a Primera Divisió . En les dues temporades següents, l’ha mantingut mantenir a la màxima categoria del futbol espanyol, fins i tot fregant les posicions de Champions. Però, el 2026 ha estat l’any per oblidar per Manolo i l’afició blanc-i-blava: patint per no baixar en el tram final de la temporada passada i fent una mala arrencada a la lliga. També et pot interessar L’Espanyol i Manolo González toquen fons a la Copa del Rei davant el Sestao River Pablo Agudo 2 minuts de lectura Situació crítica a la Lliga Actualment, l’equip espanyolista està en posicions de descens. Ocupa la divuitena posició a només un punt de la salvació. Els blanc-i-blaus només han guanyat dos partits en deu jornades, sumant vuit punts. articles.body: Jordi Amat ha estat entrevistat al bàsics , de betevé. Concretament a la secció ‘El mirador Barcelona’ , en què diferents personalitats vinculades a la ciutat en parlen. Escriptor i autor del llibre Les batalles de Barcelona , premi Bones Lletres d’assaig humanístic, Amat ha repassat les bondats i defectes de mig segle de democràcia a la ciutat i com veu la Barcelona d’avui en dia i del futur. Després de mitja vida a la Nova Esquerra de l’Eixample , i com a veí de Consell de Cent , defensa la transformació del carrer “que s’ha convertit en una rambla “. Un canvi que percep com “una esperança en aquest malestar que molts compartim sobre la deriva, en part inevitable, de la ciutat”. Que els barris siguin “un espai de trobada “, afegeix Amat, “fa que la ciutat sigui més democràtica “. També et pot interessar Toni Clapés, sobre la superilla de l’Eixample: “És un projecte insolidari i kafkià” redacció web 2 minuts de lectura “El pessimisme, democràticament, és un tòxic” Amat s’ha definit com un militant de l’optimisme perquè creu que “el pessimisme, democràticament, és un tòxic “. Tot i això, ha posat el focus en la pressió turística i la manca d’habitatge com a gran repte de futur. Per Amat, no poder viure on un treballa i on es vol arrelar “perquè els sous no t’ho permeten o no hi ha prou habitatge”, és molt més que una qüestió econòmica : “Si hem perdut la confiança que puguem viure a la nostra ciutat, tenim un problema democràtic”, ha sentenciat. L’escriptor ha posat com a exemple paradigmàtic el cas de la Casa Orsola , que considera simbòlic d’una crisi que ja no afecta només els col·lectius més vulnerables . Per Amat, “un professor que no pot viure en un barri on viu la classe mitjana “, es tracta d’un cas “completament simbòlic del problema amb què ens trobem”. articles.body: El sindicat Metges de Catalunya comença aquest dimecres una vaga indefinida . La jornada de protesta començarà amb una manifestació dels facultatius a l’avinguda Diagonal . La marxa començarà a les 9 del matí a la cruïlla amb l’avinguda del Doctor Marañón i finalitzarà a les portes del Departament de Salut, a la travessera de les Corts. Us esperem a l'Avinguda Diagonal! pic.twitter.com/W0ShxHXUXa — Metges de Catalunya (@metgescatalunya) October 23, 2026 També et pot interessar Treballadors del CAP la Sagrera denuncien la saturació del centre: “Vivim medicant-nos” Max Sagués 2 minuts de lectura Aturades només a Catalunya Inicialment l’aturada havia de coincidir amb una mobilització estatal, però la convocatòria d’eleccions generals va fer que s’ajornés, excepte a Catalunya. Metges de Catalunya considera que les reclamacions del col·lectiu atenen a qüestions que són competència de la Generalitat i mantenen la protesta. El Departament de Salut , en canvi, no ho veu així i no va assistir a la reunió de mediació convocada al Departament de Treball perquè va considerar que les reivindicacions dels facultatius queden fora de les seves competències i corresponen a l’àmbit estatal. També et pot interessar Xavier Lleonart, Metges de Catalunya: “La interlocució amb la conselleria és inexistent” Arnau Vaqué 1 minut de lectura 12 hores màxim de jornada laboral i un 20 % més de sou Metges de Catalunya ha fet una llista amb 12 reivindicacions . Així, demana reformar les guàrdies i els descansos posteriors per arribar progressivament a una jornada màxima diària de dotze hores , limitar les agendes dels metges de família a un màxim de 25 actes assistencials, presencials i no presencials, i estudiar les càrregues de treball de totes les especialitats. L’organització també reclama incrementar almenys un 20 % les retribucions dels facultatius i situar el pagament de l’hora de guàrdia, com a mínim, en el 175 % del valor de l’hora ordinària. Per als metges en formació, exigeix substituir les guàrdies de 24 hores per torns de dotze sense pèrdua retributiva i augmentar un 20 % les remuneracions a través dels complements autonòmics.

articles.body: El Sestao River podria haver posat l’últim clau al taüt futbolístic de Manolo González amb l’Espanyol . Els periquitos han perdut per 4 a 3 contra un rival de Segona RFEF i queden eliminats de la Copa del Re i a la primera ronda. Un cop duríssim per a l’equip, però sobretot per a un tècnic que, ara sí, sembla que podria tenir les hores comptades a la banqueta . Inici de somni, final de malson Arribar i moldre. Marcos Fernández només ha trigat sis minuts a obrir el marcador. El 18 periquito no ha fallat des del punt de penal i ha fet avançar l’Espanyol després d’un penal comès sobre ell mateix. La resposta, gairebé immediata, ha anat a càrrec de Jon Rojo , que ha estat a punt de treure les teranyines amb un xut que ha llepat l’escaire. El Sestao, de fet, ha passat a rondar l’àrea blanc-i-blava i ha cantat bingo. Carrión , al minut 17, ha superat Dmitrovic des de dins l’àrea per posar l’ 1 a 1 . El que havia començat com un somni, s’ha tornat malson a les acaballes de la primera part. Ugarte ha saltat més que ningú a la sortida d’un córner i ha fet el segon del Sestao . Galleda d’aigua freda per a l’Espanyol i per a un Manolo González a qui ràpidament han buscat les càmares de la retransmissió. Manolo recorre als titulars i Roberto empata al 90 Manolo González ha posat tota la carn a la graella amb l’entrada de Bryan, Roberto o Expósito entre d’altres, però no hi ha hagut res a fer. La mala dinàmica de l’Espanyol s’ho ha emportat tot per endavant i, de fet, el Sestao River podria haver ampliat distàncies. Els bascos no han patit fins al final, quan l’Espanyol ha cremat les naus i ha acabat empatant, de nou, gràcies a un penal. El 2 a 2 l’ha fet Roberto i ha enviat el partit a la pròrroga . El Sestao paga l’Espanyol amb la mateixa moneda i s’emporta el triomf A la pròrroga, Moscardo ha fet el 2 a 3 amb un bon xut des de la frontal de l’àrea al minut 96, però només un minut més tard, Castillo ha pentinat una falta lateral i ha tornat a igualar el marcador . Cabrera ha estat a punt d’evitar els penals amb una xilena espectacular que el porter local ha enviat a córner. Tot feia pensar que l’Espanyol es jugaria l’accés als penals, però al darrer sospir, una jugada embolicada, amb una badada de Dmitrovic ha acabat amb el 4 a 3 de Jon Rojo . Deliri a Sestao i cop duríssim per a l’Espanyol i per a Manolo González en concret. articles.body: Els aldarulls de dissabte passat a Barcelona han generat estupefacció tant per la seva virulència com pel fet que molts dels detinguts són menors d’edat . De fet, de les 130 detencions que van fer els Mossos, 76 corresponen a menors, alguns dels quals només tenen 14 anys. Aquesta realitat ha fet posar sobre la taula alguns interrogants, com ara què passa quan un menor és detingut per la policia? O quin paper hi juguen els progenitors? Són responsables del que hagi fet el seu fill? També et pot interessar Aldarulls de Barcelona: “Els menors estan molt manipulats per les xarxes” Marta Casals Torres 2 minuts de lectura Entrevistes amb el menor i els pares Quan la policia deté un menor ha de comunicar-ho a la fiscalia , com a màxim dins de les 24 hores posteriors al moment de l’arrest. A partir d’aquí, la fiscalia té l’obligació (si així ho considera) de posar el menor a disposició del jutge de garanties en un termini màxim de 48 h posteriors a la seva detenció. Durant aquest termini, el ministeri fiscal redacta la seva petició sobre el cas. A banda, un equip tècnic integrat per psicòlegs i treballadors socials elabora un informe —després d’ entrevistar-se amb el menor i la seva família — que després entrega al jutge. Finalment, amb tota aquesta documentació el jutge resol quines són les mesures més adients per cada cas concret. També et pot interessar Qui pagarà la factura dels comerços vandalitzats? Cristina Brotons 3 minuts de lectura “La llei del menor no busca el càstig” Tal com ha explicat en una entrevista al Bon dia, Barcelona de betevé, la jutgessa degana de Barcelona, Cristina Ferrando , “el procediment per resoldre la situació d’un detingut menor d’edat és més complex”. “En aquesta primera fase hi intervenen les famílies, perquè no només s’analitza el fet concret sinó també la situació del menor”, relata. Ferrando també explica les particularitats de la jurisdicció de menors. “No és punitiva, no busca el càstig”, explica, sinó que “a través de les mesures que s’imposin al menor es pugui integrar en un futur a la societat en les millors condicions”. “Això no vol dir que les accions no tinguin conseqüències”, aclareix. Els pares, responsables econòmicament? I què passa amb els pares? Són responsables dels actes del seu fill menor? Han de respondre econòmicament als danys que hagi ocasionat? L’expert en seguretat Amadeu Recasens ha explicat al Bon dia, Barcelona , de betevé, que el grau de responsabilitat és en funció de l’edat del menor. Així, els menors de 14 anys són inimputables penalment , però en canvi els pares tenen una responsabilitat directa i subsidiària en el cas que s’aconsegueixi provar els fets. “Els pares són responsables econòmicament de les destrosses” , alerta. Entre els 14 i els 18 anys els menors sí que són penalment responsables . És a dir, tenen una responsabilitat legal (tot i que atenuada) i s’han de fer càrrec dels danys que provoquen. Finalment, a partir dels 18 anys ja hi ha una responsabilitat penal i patrimonial plena. També et pot interessar Què hi ha rere els aldarulls a Barcelona? Els experts analitzen el fenomen Max Sagués 2 minuts de lectura La Generalitat es personarà com a acusació De moment, en espera de les actuacions judicials, la Generalitat ja ha anunciat que es personarà com a acusació particular, tant pels danys a l’espai públic que es van produir durant els aldarulls, com per les lesions a agents dels Mossos d’Esquadra. La portaveu, Sílvia Paneque, ha afirmat que els mossos continuen investigant qui hi ha al darrera de la convocatòria que es va fer través de xarxes socials i ha dit que el govern català “posarà tots els mecanismes perquè aquests espais no es converteixin en espais d’impunitat”.

articles.body: (ACN) El govern es personarà com a acusació particular pels aldarulls del cap de setmana a Barcelona. articles.body: (ACN) La Generalitat i Renfe han formalitzat aquest dimarts el contracte programa que fixa les condicions econòmiques i de prestació del servei ferroviari de Rodalies i Regionals fins a finals del 2028. Es tracta d’un document que estava pendent des de feia 15 anys, des del traspàs parcial de la gestió de Rodalies a Catalunya el 2010. El document preveu un pressupost de 1.407,6 milions d’euros en tres anys, en què s’inclou un màxim de cinc milions anuals en compensacions per impuntualitat i els 74 milions que va costar la gratuïtat del servei després de l’accident de Gelida. Tot, sortirà de les arques de l’Estat. La portaveu del govern, Sílvia Paneque , ha defensat que és un acord que “ordena” el servei i que permet a la Generalitat exercici com a titular amb “més capacitat” . A parer seu, el document dona “estabilitat” i “seguretat jurídica” i formalitza una relació que ja existia, però que no tenia un acord per escrit. També et pot interessar Puente defensa que el traspàs de Rodalies continua, tot i que el 29-N pot alterar el calendari Marina Sancho 1 minut de lectura El document, però, encara està pendent d’un pas final perquè estigui vigent: ha de passar per la Comissió Mixta d’Afers Econòmics i Fiscals Estat-Generalitat (Cmaef), un tràmit que el govern preveu que es pugui completar abans del 29 de novembre, la data de les eleccions generals. Un contracte que fixa les regles del servei L’acord manté les condicions actuals del servei, però marca les regles del joc i deixa per escrit les condicions econòmiques i tècniques de la prestació ferroviària. En concret, cobreix la totalitat dels serveis de Rodalies i Regionals, tot i que preveu que les línies RL3 i RL4 surtin del contracte quan les comencin a operar els FGC. No inclou l’alta velocitat. Un altre dels compromisos inclosos en l’acord és la renovació dels trens, amb 110 noves unitats: 72 de gran capacitat per a Rodalies, 24 per als serveis Regionals i 14 trens de la sèrie 121 procedents d’altres serveis de Renfe. En matèria d’incidències, el contracte recull que Renfe haurà d’activar un Pla alternatiu de transport per carretera si l’afectació supera els 90 minuts, com fins ara, i fixa que l’operador ha de mantenir informats als usuaris i a la Generalitat. La comissió de seguiment estarà formada per sis representants, tres de la Generalitat i tres de Renfe, i assumirà les funcions de coordinació i control que fins ara exercia l’òrgan mixt Generalitat-Renfe. El contracte tindrà vigència fins al 31 de desembre del 2028 . La previsió és que aquest sigui l’últim contracte programa amb Renfe, ja que el següent hauria de formalitzar-se amb l’empresa mixta Rodalies de Catalunya , que la Generalitat preveu que estigui disponible durant el primer trimestre del 2029. articles.body: L’ RFEF ha multat el Barça pel cas Julián Álvarez i haurà de pagar una petita multa econòmica. Tot plegat després que l’ RFEF obrís un expedient al club blaugrana a finals de juliol per una denúncia de l’ Atlètic de Madrid. El club matalasser es va emparar en la normativa de la Federació , en què diu que si un club està interessat en un jugador, primer ho ha de fer saber al club afectat. El Barça recorrerà contra la decisió . El Barça haurà de pagar una petita quantitat econòmica a la Reial Federació Espanyola de Futbol per “tocar” un jugador amb un contracte en vigor, com és el cas de Julián Álvarez amb l’ Atlètic de Madrid al llarg del passat mercat de fitxatges. L’equip madrileny va posar una denúncia a la Federació perquè consideraven que el Barça vulnerava el Reglament de Competicions de la mateixa RFEF , que fa inviable iniciar negociacions amb un jugador si el seu club ho desconeix. El Barça recorrerà contra la decisió Tot i que la multa imposada per la Federació no és una gran quantitat, el club blaugrana recorrerà contra la decisió. La directiva considera que, per principis morals, té la obligació de reclamar la sanció davant l’ RFEF . Per tant, encara no és ferma la sanció econòmica imposada per l’organisme espanyol. També et pot interessar Lamine Yamal guanya el trofeu al millor talent jove per tercer any consecutiu Redacció Esports 2 minuts de lectura No és la primera vegada El cas Julián Álvarez no és l’únic que acaba amb una denúncia a l’organisme espanyol per aquest motiu. Precisament, el darrer precedent també va involucrar el Barça i l’Atlético . Va ser l’any 2019 amb el cas Antoine Griezmann. De fet, el desenllaç va ser el mateix, els blaugrana van haver de pagar una multa a la Federació . Però a diferència de Julián , el davanter francès sí que va acabar recalant a Barcelona .

articles.body: En el límit perimetral que conformava la barriada de les Cases Barates , l’any 1931 va inaugurar-se el primer centre escolar de la zona que avui coneixem com el Bon Pastor: el Grup Escolar Bonaventura Carles Aribau . Amb el nom del pare de la Renaixença catalana per bandera, aquest centre va suposar un bri d’esperança per un barri majoritàriament analfabet i amb poc coneixement de la nostra llengua. D’aquesta manera, part la rellevància d’aquesta escola radica en què va ser la que va permetre instaurar el català en una àrea poblada per més d’un 85 % de migrants vinguts d’arreu d’Espanya. Clau per la progressió del barri Tot plegat forma part del recull historiogràfic fet per Josep Capsir, autor del llibre Les Cases Barates i el Grup Escolar Bonaventura Carles Aribau 1931-1939 , una obra que aborda els orígens del Bon Pastor a partir de la influència que va tenir aquest centre, inaugurat ara fa 95 anys . “Va ser de vital importància”, relata Capsir, que considera que, si no és per aquesta escola, els seus més de 900 alumnes “no haurien après a desenvolupar-se”. També et pot interessar El Bon Pastor, bastió republicà a través d’un recorregut viu pel passat històric del barri Max Sagués 3 minuts de lectura Fent ús de la llei de la II República , es van aplicar ensenyament bilingüístics, el que va permetre que l’alumnat “normalitzés l’ús del català” en el seu dia a dia. A banda, l’obertura d’aquest centre va implicar altres novetats, com ara la introducció de mètodes pedagògics d’arreu d’Europa . La pedagogia francesa de Freinet, amb l’ús de la impremta a les aules per part dels alumnes —els quals van crear la seva pròpia revista reivindicativa —, va ser la que més va amarar. “Desenllaç nefast” Tot i la implicació dels seus directors Concepció Tudó i Llorenç Jou, el futur prolífic que s’augurava per aquesta escola no va poder superar els obstacles que la Guerra Civil va anar deixant pel camí. Així, amb l’arribada de les tropes franquistes a Barcelona el gener del 1939 es va anul·lar el Patronat Escolar de Barcelona, i amb ell va desmuntar-se el sistema educatiu que sostentava aquest grup escolar, que va ser clausurat. articles.body: (ACN) La Confederació de Sindicats de Llogateres, FACUA i Justícia Alimentària han cridat a fer una “vaga de compres” a les grans superfícies tots els dimecres fins a l’ aturada general de l’11 de novembre . Les tres organitzacions demanen “ no comprar en supermercats, hipermercats ni grans cadenes ” aquest dimecres, 28 d’octubre, i el 4 de novembre i fer-ho en mercats municipals, comerços de barri, cooperatives o directament a productores . També et pot interessar El Sindicat de Llogateres i estudiants “ocupen” la UB per preparar la vaga de l’11-N Redacció 1 minut de lectura Cap compra el dia de l’aturada general Les organitzacions demanen “no fer cap compra” l’11-N, dia de la vaga general, ni en establiments físics ni per internet. En un comunicat conjunt, expliquen que volen denunciar que el cistell de consum ha pujat de preu “molt més que els sous” . També coincideixen a dir que “treballar ja no garanteix arribar a final de mes”. En el comunicat, asseguren que mentrestant “uns pocs baten rècords de beneficis amb el que cal per viure, un sostre i un plat a taula”. Segons els seus càlculs, el cistell de consum s’ha encarit un 40 % des del 2019, mentre que els salaris s’han incrementat un 21,9 % en el mateix període .
